source: City of Helsinki, Luontotietojärjestelmä (Nature Information System)
licence_proof: Helsinki's general open geographic data page states maps and geographic data created by the City of Helsinki's City Survey Services are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, attribution "Data and maps (c) City of Helsinki, City Survey Services"; independently confirmed by the dataset's own listing on avoindata.suomi.fi for "Helsingin luontotietojärjestelmä", which names Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License by name. Scouted and fetched 2026-08-23.
designation: luonnonmuistomerkki (natural monument), individually protected under the Nature Conservation Act or by the city's own municipal decision (see huom field per entry: several are protected by municipal decision rather than the Act, which does not affect their status as an official designation, only which legal basis applies)
attribution: City of Helsinki, City Survey Services
scope: 23 individual trees or small tree groups kept from the WFS layer's 31 total features. 8 excluded as geological features (hiidenkirnu "giant's kettles", a rock crevice, a boulder/outcrop), which share the luonnonmuistomerkki designation with trees in Helsinki but are not trees at all. 1 excluded (Kaksi koivua, Kulosaari, id 27) because its own kuvaus states it stands on a private plot (yksityisellä tontilla), failing hard rule 10.
caveat: THIN ON DESCRIPTIVE FIELDS: only one of the 23 kept entries (Kuninkaan tammi / King's Oak, id 4) carries a free-text kuvaus; the rest give only a Finnish common name (often just the species, e.g. "Mänty" = Scots pine, "Tammi" = oak) and a neighbourhood, no age, girth or height anywhere in this feature class. A verify pass must find age/girth/second-source facts elsewhere (Helsinki city tree registers, local press, on-the-ground description); this register alone establishes existence, common species and a council-designated remarkable status, which counts as one official-register source under this project's two-source rule. The King's Oak (id 4) needs an access check before it can ship: its own kuvaus places it "vesilaitoksen omistaman tilan pihassa" (in the yard of a property owned by the water utility), which is not obviously open to casual visitors and needs the same per-candidate judgement CLAUDE.md applies to school/company grounds before it clears hard rule 10, not an automatic yes or no. All other entries read as ordinary public park/street locations by their neighbourhood names (Tullisaari, Seurasaari, Tali etc are public parks and islands) but have not been individually access-checked here either; treat as leads until a verify pass confirms each one.
